idiomatic.rationale: Config, routing, 404 handling and components read like the framework's own examples; the only real deviation is a bespoke partial-swap layer for filter/sort updates instead of Astro's router, plus global rather than scoped CSS (permitted by the spec).

correctness_risks.rationale: No serious bugs: abort controllers handle the fetch races, escaping is left to Astro, 404s are handled everywhere, and the cache is rejection-safe. What remains are minor robustness gaps — no upstream-error page, page-clamp/URL desync, and a too-greedy live region.

evidence: app/src/lib/api.ts:33 — reviewer nit: cache TTL stamped at request time, so slow responses eat into it

app/src/pages/index.astro:159 — popstate/focus edge case and the live-region nit above are one-line fixes

review_cost.rationale: I'd approve after one round of nits: add an error page, fix the live region and page-clamp desync, and stop the card component from emitting its own list item. Nothing needs rework.

findings.issue: Non-404 upstream failures throw out of getJson and surface as an unstyled 500 with a stack trace; no page handles it.
findings.suggestion: Add a src/pages/500.astro (or catch errors in a small wrapper around getJson) that renders a friendly error page with the site chrome.

findings.issue: aria-live="polite" on the container that holds all 48 cards and pagination makes screen readers announce the whole region on every keystroke-driven update.
findings.suggestion: Move aria-live to the small '<count> Pokémon' status element (or a dedicated visually-hidden status region) and leave the card list unannounced.

findings.issue: Out-of-range or non-numeric ?page is clamped server-side while the URL keeps the invalid value, so the address bar and rendered view disagree.
findings.suggestion: Redirect to the clamped URL (Astro.redirect) when the requested page is outside 1..totalPages, or leave the raw value out of pagination links.

findings.issue: The card component renders its own <li>, so it only works when a parent supplies <ul>; four call sites currently do, but the constraint is implicit.
findings.suggestion: Render only the link (and let each page own the list item), or document the requirement in the component's Props comment.

findings.issue: The global cache Map grows without bound and expired entries are only replaced lazily on access; a long-lived server with a changing API would accumulate entries indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Sweep expired entries on insert (or cap the Map size); the dataset is fixed today, but this is a two-line guard.

findings.issue: popstate sync skips document.activeElement, so a focused search input can show stale text after back/forward navigation.
findings.suggestion: Sync the focused element too, or blur the input before syncing when the URL's q differs from its value.

findings.issue: tsconfig extends astro/tsconfigs/strict but the code is full of any (getJson<T = any>, (a: any) casts in pokemon/[name].astro) and astro check is never run — the strictness is cosmetic.
findings.suggestion: Add @astrojs/check as a devDependency with a check script, and type the API payloads (at least the fields actually read) instead of any.

findings.issue: A hand-rolled fetch + DOMParser + innerHTML partial-swap duplicates what Astro's view-transitions router provides, and requires the data-results region's markup to stay hand-synced with the server template.
findings.suggestion: Consider the ClientRouter (view transitions) so navigation and form-driven updates share one framework-maintained swap path; at minimum, extract the swap helper so index.astro and MoveTables.astro don't each carry their own copy.

findings.issue: getSpeciesById returns a Map<number, string> of names, which the name doesn't convey; getPokemonIndex bundles a home-page-shaped triple into the shared module.
findings.suggestion: Rename to getSpeciesNamesById and move getPokemonIndex's assembly into the home page (or a home-scoped module) to keep lib/api.ts a pure data layer.

findings.issue: history.pushState is called with the #moves hash still on the URL, then the hash is stripped only from the local copy used for the fetch — correct but subtle enough to trip a future editor.
findings.suggestion: Build the fetch URL and the history URL as two explicitly named variables (fetchUrl / historyUrl) so the intent is obvious.

summary: This is a clean, idiomatic Astro 7 SSR app I'd merge after one round of nits: correct config and adapter, file-based routing with proper 404 handling, a well-bounded data module, and small focused components. The main things I'd ask for are an error page for upstream API failures, a less chatty live region, and dropping the component-level any-typing in favour of actually running astro check. The one structural habit worth watching is the hand-rolled partial-swap layer, which reimplements what the framework's router already does and must be kept in sync by hand.
